    Slay the Spire 2 Cards overview

    Slay the Spire 2 cards are the core of your deckbuilder run. Every character — Ironclad, Silent, Defect, Necrobinder, and the Regent — has a unique card pool with its own mechanics, plus a shared set of Colorless and Quest cards that appear across multiple runs. This Slay the Spire 2 card database lets you browse every card by character, type, rarity, and energy cost.

    Use the filters and character tabs above to focus on the card pool you care about most. Whether you are planning an Ironclad Strength deck, a Silent discard-combo build, a Defect Orb engine, a Necrobinder Doom setup, or a Regent Stars and Forge shell, this Slay the Spire 2 card list is built to be quickly scannable while you theorycraft.

    Card types and rarities in Slay the Spire 2

    Slay the Spire 2 cards still follow the classic Attack, Skill, and Power types, but each character also adds twists through mechanics like Sly, Doom, Stars, and Orbs. Cards come in Common, Uncommon, Rare, and special rarities such as Quest and Colorless. Rarity hints at power, but the strongest cards are those that fit your deck&apos;s plan and energy curve, not just the ones with gold borders.

    Building a consistent deck with this card list

    Consistency wins runs. When browsing this Slay the Spire 2 card database, pay attention to how many cheap cards, scaling pieces, defensive tools, and payoff cards you are taking. Aim for an energy curve that lets you reliably play your hand every turn, rather than stuffing your deck with expensive, situational cards that clog your draws.

    Slay the Spire 2 Cards FAQ

    How many cards should be in my deck?

    There is no perfect number, but thinner decks are usually more consistent. In Slay the Spire 2, try to remove low-impact starter cards and avoid adding mediocre choices just because they are offered. Use this card list to identify which Slay the Spire 2 cards are true upgrades for your current deck, and skip the rest.

    Should I prioritize upgrades or new cards?

    Upgrading key cards can be more valuable than adding new ones, especially for core payoff cards, scaling engines, and crucial defensive tools. Use this card database to compare base and upgraded versions of important Slay the Spire 2 cards, then decide whether your next campfire should be a Rest or a Smith.

    How do character mechanics change card evaluation?

    Each character&apos;s unique mechanics — Sly, Doom, Stars, Orbs, and more — dramatically shift how strong certain cards become. A card that looks weak in isolation can be incredible when combined with the right relics or supporting pieces. As you browse this Slay the Spire 2 card list, always evaluate cards in the context of your current synergies instead of using fixed tier lists.

    Planning routes and fights around your cards

    Using this card list to spot missing pieces

    Before major decisions — shops, elites, or boss fights — use this Slay the Spire 2 card list to check which tools your deck is missing. If you lack scalable damage, look for cards that add Strength, multi-hit attacks, or repeatable sources of damage. If your defense is weak, prioritize reliable Block cards, scaling defensive Powers, or cards that thin your deck.

    Aligning pathing with your card plan

    Your route should follow your deck&apos;s needs. If you see many potential upgrades and synergistic Slay the Spire 2 cards in this database, you can safely path toward more elites and events. If your deck is fragile or incomplete, favour shops, removals, and safer fights until you lock in a coherent plan. Let the card pool you are aiming for guide how risky your pathing should be.
